questions.question: Which folder does Claude Code work in?

options.text: The folder where you started it
options.explanation: Correct. That’s why you first move to the project folder with the cd command and only then start Claude.
Claude Code works in the folder where it was started.

options.text: Only in the cloud, not on your own computer
options.explanation: Claude Code edits files on your own computer. That’s why it asks for permission.

questions.question: Claude started doing something you didn’t mean. What do you do?

options.text: I press Esc and explain more precisely what I want
options.explanation: Exactly. Esc stops the work, and you can steer Claude in the right direction.

options.text: I turn off the computer with the power button
options.explanation: Far too drastic. Esc is enough, and the work done so far is kept.

options.text: I wait and hope for the best
options.explanation: You’re at the controls. Interrupt and clarify, that’s completely normal.

questions.question: How do you quit Claude Code?

options.explanation: An ordinary message goes to Claude as part of the conversation. You quit the program with the command /exit.
Correct. Commands that start with a slash are Claude Code’s own commands.
/help shows the instructions. You quit with the command /exit.
